ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High contrast ratio with approximately 45% high-intensity pixels (white/yellowish regions) and 55% low-intensity pixels (black/dark grey regions) visible across the exposed ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Two primary high-intensity contiguous blobs located on the lateral lobes, tapering towards the tips. The central peduncle region and the entire perimeter of the trailing edge consist of low-intensity black pixels. High-intensity areas show internal mottling and pixel-level gradients to yellowish-white.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Distinct acute V-shaped depression with a calculated internal angle of approximately 55 degrees; depth is significant, extending approximately 10% of the fluke's vertical height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration; peaks and valleys are most prominent on the inner half of each lobe, decreasing in amplitude toward the lateral tips.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly convex trailing edge curve on both lobes, terminating in sharp, slightly swept-back distal tips.

other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced yellowish-tan tinting localized within the high-intensity white pixel regions, suggesting non-pigmentary surface accumulation (diatom film).
